ready-cap-note: `head-rule` is the string "none" — the schema allows that and this repo has no lead goal. `ready-cap` is left NULL and FAILING on purpose: the schema demands a positive integer, R22 withdrew caps entirely, and there is no honest number. Fabricating one to reach a green would be the label-wearing-a-measurement's-clothes defect R22 exists to prevent. The finding is the schema lag, and the growth-control wave removes the key.

items.staleness: change-coupling — an item whose evidence or requirement record pointer no longer resolves

exit.detail: to ITEMS-DONE.md on DONE or DROPPED

items.bound: bounded-by-exit — every item leaves by a recorded closure or a recorded drop; growth is watched by flow (a kind that grew without an exit event), never by a cap (R22)

done bodies.writer: tool — lifecycle item close, the atomic move; no other writer
done bodies.staleness: none, declared why: a closure record is history — it accumulates, it does not go stale

exit.recording-act: a ledger decision line naming the compacted range
exit.detail: WAVE 4 — declared now so the kind has no undeclared stage, not implemented

done bodies.bound: compacted — the archive's control is compaction rather than a bound; unbounded until the retire lane exists, declared why: this is history and dropping it would lose the basis of laws still in force

ledger lines.writer: tool for the slots, session for the reason prose
reader: the grade workflow's ledger rejected --for gate
ledger lines.staleness: none, declared why: append-only decision history

exit.recording-act: compaction only — a line whose item is DONE and past the horizon folds into that body's compaction line

ledger lines.bound: unbounded-with-reason — one line per decision event, no bodies; the decision rate is the control

journal entries.writer: session — an incident and its lesson, written by the session that had it
reader: the law or workflow that cites the entry as its basis
journal entries.staleness: change-coupling — an entry nothing cites is stale, and a law carrying no journal pointer has no basis; read against the citing artifact, never against the entry's age

exit.recording-act: the citing law's pointer is the record; an entry leaves only through the retire lane's compaction, which names the folded range in a ledger decision line

journal entries.bound: unbounded-with-reason — one entry per incident, so growth is bounded by the incident rate; a cap here would drop the lesson justifying a law still in force

audits.writer: session — one measurement per file, written once and not revised
reader: the item whose evidence slot cites the audit
audits.staleness: change-coupling — an audit whose measured artifact has moved past the citation it carries no longer measures anything current

exit.recording-act: none is taken: append-only historical; the recording act for a superseded measurement is the newer audit citing the one it overtakes

audits.bound: unbounded-with-reason — one file per measurement; a measurement is only taken when a question needs it, and that is the control

refusal-registry.writer: session — a row is added beside the guard it defends, and proven red by tools/prove-rows.py before it counts
reader: design §3.9's table, which is a SNAPSHOT of this registry and updates from it, never the reverse
refusal-registry.staleness: emit-site coverage — a registry that has fallen behind the code is detected by the coverage check, which reads the SOURCE for finding-emitting sites and fails when one maps to no registered row

exit.recording-act: a row leaves only by deletion with a ledger line naming why — including the deletion of an UNPROVABLE row, which is law 22's case

refusal-registry.bound: bounded-by-exit — a row enters with its firing input and leaves only by a recorded deletion; the roster's own output states how much of itself is proven, so growth without proof is visible rather than silent

workflow-template.writer: session — via a reviewed PR, never an in-place edit: a template is extracted from a PRIVATE repo into a PUBLISHED one and the leak scan runs on that boundary
reader: the per-repo template-bindings in each declaring repo's declaration
workflow-template.staleness: no binder — a template no repo binds is stale by definition; the plugin's suite runs every template against every binder, so a binding that stops resolving is loud

exit.recording-act: a dependents search over every declaring repo's template-bindings FIRST, then a ledger line naming the retired template and the repos that had bound it. Encoded as `delete` because the closed exit vocabulary is move|compact|delete|never and 'retire' is not in it — the dependents search is the recording act, not a fifth action

workflow-template.bound: unbounded-with-reason — one per shared procedure, and a procedure is only shared once two or more lanes use it; the sharing threshold is the control, not a count
